intro_html: Loco moco is Hawaii's diner classic: a seared beef patty on rice, drowned in savory gravy, with a fried egg on top. Each bowl delivers 39 grams of protein for about $2.17. Comfort food math that actually works in your favor.
cost_closing_html: About $2.17 a bowl for a plate lunch that runs $15 at any Hawaiian barbecue spot on the mainland. The gravy is flour, drippings, and broth, which is to say nearly free.
shop_smart: Eggs at about 12 cents each are the cheapest way to dress up a bowl and add protein while you are at it. Fourteen of them cost less than one restaurant egg upcharge.
The gravy comes from pan drippings, butter, flour, beef broth, and a splash of soy, roughly 30 cents a bowl. A jar of premade gravy costs more and tastes worse.
Beef is the whole bill here at $21.60, so pin this recipe to the week the 4 lb pack of 93/7 goes on sale.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Form the ground beef into 14 thin patties and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Sear the patties in the olive oil in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through with no pink in the center. Set aside, leaving the drippings.
Make the gravy in the same pan: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the beef broth and soy sauce and simmer until it coats a spoon.
Fry the eggs in a nonstick pan until the whites are set.
Portion rice into 14 containers, add a patty, ladle gravy over, and top each with a fried egg and sliced green onions.
portion_html: Weigh the rice pot, subtract the empty pot number, and divide by 14 for the base, then give each container one patty, one egg, and an even ladle of gravy. Each bowl lands at about 647 calories and 39 grams of protein.

steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Form 14 seasoned beef patties and sear in batches until cooked through.
Make gravy in the drippings with butter, flour, beef broth, and soy sauce.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Layer rice, patty, gravy, fried egg, and green onions into 14 containers.
